TIAGO FERRÃO-LINDQVIST
Data Engineering | Test & Validation Engineer (Mechanical)
tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

CURRICULUM VITAE

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation across automotive and industrial components. Builds Python tools to process test-rig data, validate results against specifications and generate reports, reducing report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. Uses SQL Server for trend analysis and MATLAB/Simulink for engineering models. Interested in moving into data engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib) | SQL / SQL Server | MATLAB/Simulink | Excel/VBA | Power BI | LabVIEW | Minitab | ANSYS Mechanical | SolidWorks | CATIA V5 | Design of Experiments (DOE) | GD&T | DFMEA | 8D problem solving

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components — Seat structures and seat-adjuster mechanisms
Setúbal | Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare test reports for OEM customers.
- Developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to read rig output files, check each channel against the test specification and generate standard report figures. Reduced report preparation time from about three days to half a day per test.
- Query the plant’s test-results database in SQL Server for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Correlate rig results with FEA in ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures. Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive, used to select rig load profiles.

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps — Industrial centrifugal pumps
Porto | Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and produced GD&T production drawings; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Conducted structural FEA of casings in ANSYS. Supported the change of one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile iron, saving 12% in material cost.
- Supported the conversion of the pump performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup using Siemens S7.

EDUCATION
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)


COVER LETTER

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role at Halden Pay. Over 12 years in mechanical engineering, I have built practical data-processing tools and used test-results data to support reliable decisions. I am now looking to move into data engineering, bringing a strong foundation in Python, SQL and data validation.

At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts that read test-rig output, validate every channel against specifications and generate standard report figures. This reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. I also query a SQL Server database to analyse trends across three product generations. This work has taught me the value of repeatable processes, clear data checks and outputs that colleagues can use with confidence—principles that align with Halden Pay’s focus on shared, reusable platform frameworks and data quality.

My experience has been in engineering data rather than operating a cloud data platform. I would bring to the Data Platform team hands-on Python and SQL experience, a disciplined approach to validating data, and a track record of improving a recurring workflow. Halden Pay’s emphasis on ownership and simplifying work to move quickly also resonates with the way I approach engineering problems: identify the source of an issue, develop a practical improvement and verify its impact.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s data platform and its users across analytics, data science and product teams. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

critique.improvement_instructions: This draft repeats the CV (in whole or in part) before or around the cover letter. Delete every part of the CV from it: its sections, headings, bullet lists, dates and skill lists. Keep only the cover letter itself (with its own header, if it has one), unchanged. The CV is sent as a separate document.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, concise, and well structured. It uses specific evidence from the candidate's experience, especially the reduction in report preparation time from about three days to half a day per test. The letter is also commendably honest about the candidate's transition from engineering data to data engineering, avoiding unsupported claims about cloud platforms or production data platforms. The connection to Halden Pay's ownership, simplification, data quality, and reusable-framework themes is credible, although the letter could make the transferable technical stack slightly more explicit.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS- and parser-friendly: it uses standard headings-free letter formatting, readable paragraphs, conventional text, and no tables, columns, graphics, or unusual symbols. It includes relevant supported keywords such as Python, SQL, data validation, data quality, data platform, reusable frameworks, and engineering data. However, it does not include the more specific supported tool names from the CV, such as pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and SQL Server. Strict screening for senior data-platform experience will likely be limited because the document accurately does not claim Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, Docker, CI/CD, dimensional modelling, or production data-platform operations. The likely AI screening outcome is moderate for transferable Python/SQL and data-quality relevance, but low to moderate for the full senior Data Engineer – Data Platform requirement set.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the candidate's genuine experience and presents a credible transition narrative. It demonstrates Python-based processing of test-rig data, validation against specifications, report automation, SQL Server trend analysis, and measurable process improvement. It also connects these capabilities to data quality and reusable platform principles, and it references Halden Pay's Ownership and Pace values appropriately. The candidate's professional English and native Portuguese are supported by the original information. The candidate material does not show production data-platform or cloud-warehouse experience at scale, advanced SQL query optimisation on large datasets, dimensional or graph modelling, hands-on Google Cloud or comparable cloud experience, or open-source/data-architecture experience. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects in the letter.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second paragraph, change the first sentence to make the supported technical stack more searchable and precise: "At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy and Matplotlib to read test-rig output, validate every channel against specifications and generate standard report figures." In the following SQL sentence, change "I also query a SQL Server database" to "I also query a SQL Server test-results database". This adds exact supported keywords without implying cloud, platform-scale, or advanced query-optimisation experience.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Strong data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
